question: My employer mentions an ROE and Service Canada following a layoff in Canada. What benefits program are they referring to, and must I wait until all paperwork is gathered to apply?
generated_answer: The ROE is a document that your employer must provide to you when your employment ends. It contains information about your employment history, including the dates of your employment, your salary, and any other relevant details. The ROE is used by Service Canada to determine your eligibility for certain benefits, such as Employment Insurance (EI) and the Canada Pension Plan (CPP). You do not need to wait until all paperwork is gathered to apply for benefits. You can apply for EI as soon as you receive your ROE, and you can apply for CPP at any time. However, you will need to provide your ROE as part of the application process.
